comment: One-line descriptions and usage snippets mined by tools/language/reference.mjs --generate from the built manual (doc/html/r3_*.html) and the twin fixtures (tests/pov4). Descriptions carry the manual anchor they were taken from; absent words were not found. Block one-liners and 4.0-only words live in overlay.json. Regenerate rather than edit.

aa_level.text: You can specify the anti-aliasing recursion depth using the aa_level keyword followed by an integer.

aa_threshold.text: You can specify the anti-aliasing threshold by using the aa_threshold followed by a float.

absorption.text: The absorption keyword specifies a color of light which is absorbed when looking through the media.

accuracy.text: For this reason, a new property, accuracy, has been added to normals.

adaptive.text: The adaptive keyword is used to enable adaptive sampling of the light source.

adc_bailout.text: You may use the global setting adc_bailout keyword followed by float value to specify the point at which a ray's contribution is considered insignificant.

agate.text: The agate pattern is a banded pattern similar to marble but it uses a specialized built-in turbulence function that is different from the traditional turbulence.

agate_turb.text: The agate_turb modifier can only be used with the agate pattern.

albedo.text: The optional keyword albedo can be used right after diffuse to specify that the parameter is to be taken as the total diffuse/specular reflectance, rather than peak reflectance.

all.text: The only restriction is that shadowless should be before or after all spotlight or cylinder option keywords.

all_intersections.text: To check for all surfaces, use the keyword all_intersections instead.

always_sample.text: Since always_sample off is the default, POV-Ray will only use the data from the pretrace step and not gather any new samples during the final radiosity pass.

ambient.text: The ambient keyword controls the amount of ambient light used for each object.

ambient_light.text: POV-Ray provides the ambient_light keyword to let you easily change the brightness of the ambient lighting without changing every ambient value in all finish statements.

angle.text: The viewing angle can be specified by using the angle keyword.

aoi.text: The aoi pattern can be used with pigment, normal and texture statements.

aperture.text: To turn on focal blur, you must specify the aperture keyword followed by a float value which determines the depth of the sharpness zone.

area_illumination.text: The array-effect applies to shadows only, however with the addition of the area_illumination keyword, full area light diffuse and specular illumination can be achieved.

area_light.text: The area_light keyword in POV-Ray creates sources that are rectangular in shape, sort of like a flat panel light.

atmosphere.text: Earlier versions of POV-Ray used an atmosphere statement for atmospheric effects but that system was incompatible with the old object halo system.

atmospheric_ior.text: A scene set under water with atmospheric_ior 1.33 refracts at a glass ball of ior 1.5 by 1.5 / 1.33, as it would inside a large water object.

autostop.text: To understand the autostop option, you need to understand the way photons are shot from light sources.

average.text: Technically average is not a pattern type but it is listed here because the syntax is similar to other patterns.

blur_samples.text: You must also specify the blur_samples keyword followed by an integer value specifying the maximum number of rays to use for each pixel.

bokeh.text: If bokeh is specified, focal blur will use a custom sampling sequence based on the specified pigment's brightness in the range <0,0,0> to <1,1,0> i.e.

bounded_by.text: While it may a good idea to manually add a bounded_by to intersection, difference and merge, it is best to never bound a union.

boxed.text: The boxed pattern creates a 2x2x2 unit cube centered at the origin.

bozo.text: The bozo pattern is a very smooth, random noise function that is traditionally used with some turbulence to create clouds.

brick.text: The brick pattern generates a pattern of bricks.

brick_size.text: These values may be changed using the optional brick_size and mortar pattern modifiers.

brightness.text: A brightness value is followed by an optional unit, written after the number; the unit words nits and lumens are read only there and stay free as identifiers.

brilliance.text: The brilliance keyword can be used in a finish statement to vary the way light falls off depending upon the angle of incidence.

bump_size.text: Originally bump_size could only be used inside a bump map but it can now be used with any normal.

bumps.text: The bumps pattern was originally designed only to be used as a normal pattern.

caustics.text: The caustics Power keyword controls the effect.

cells.text: The cells pattern fills 3d space with unit cubes.

charset.text: Refer to your platform specific documentation if you specified charset sys.

checker.text: The checker pattern produces a checkered pattern consisting of alternating squares of two colors.

chr.text: Character whose character value is B.

circular.text: The circular keyword has been added to area lights in order to better create circular soft shadows.

clipped_by.text: The clipped_by statement is technically an object modifier but it provides a type of CSG similar to CSG intersection.

collect.text: The keyword collect off causes the object to ignore photons.

color_map.text: The colors are defined in a pigment modifier called a color_map that describes how the pattern blends from one color to the next.

colour_map.text: The colors are defined in a pigment modifier called a color_map that describes how the pattern blends from one color to the next.

component.text: The component keyword is an obsolete method for specifying a spherical component and is only used for compatibility with earlier POV-Ray versions.

confidence.text: The confidence and variance keywords are followed by float values to control the adaptive function.

conserve_energy.text: This can be achieved by adding the conserve_energy keyword to the object's finish {}.

control0.text: The two parameters control0 and control1 are used to adjust the curvature of the seam or gouge area between the quilts.

control1.text: The two parameters control0 and control1 are used to adjust the curvature of the seam or gouge area between the quilts.

coords.text: If coords is specified, the facets pattern creates facets with a size on the same order as the specified SCALE_VALUE.

crackle.text: The crackle pattern is a set of random tiled multifaceted cells.

crand.text: The crand keyword can be added to a finish to cause a minor random darkening in the diffuse reflection of direct illumination.

cylindrical.text: The cylindrical pattern creates a one unit radius cylinder along the Y axis.

datetime.text: Can be used to return the string representation of a date and time.

density_file.text: The density_file pattern is a 3-D bitmap pattern that occupies a unit cube from location <0,0,0> to <1,1,1>.

density_map.text: The DENSITY_LIST and density_map modifiers only work with media{density{..}} statements.

dents.text: The dents pattern was originally designed only to be used as a normal pattern.

detail.text: Per-field detail D is a finite positive length in scene units; omitted detail or detail auto uses bounds-derived preparation and integration controls.

diffuse.text: The keyword diffuse is used in a finish statement to control how much of the light coming directly from any light sources is reflected via diffuse reflection.

direction.text: A shorter direction vector gives a wider view while a longer vector zooms in for close-ups.

dispersion.text: In order to get a more realistic effect the dispersion and dispersion_samples keywords can be added to the interior{} block.

dispersion_samples.text: In order to get a more realistic effect the dispersion and dispersion_samples keywords can be added to the interior{} block.

distance.text: The required distance keyword is the same like the one used with fogs.

double_illuminate.text: When double_illuminate is used, the other side is also illuminated.

eccentricity.text: This eccentricity is specified by the optional keyword eccentricity which is only used for scattering type five.

error_bound.text: The error_bound float value is one of the two main speed/quality tuning values (the other is of course the number of rays shot).

exit.text: Without exit, a view through a portal carries on into the target for as far as it goes.

exponent.text: As a means to work around the phenomenon the optional exponent keyword was added, producing non-linear reflection intensities.

exterior.text: The form, exterior and interior specify the look of angle used for respectively slow convex (turning side), quick convex (pointy tile) and concave angle (interior angle between many tiles).

face_indices.text: To do this, specify the smooth triangles first in the face_indices section, followed by the flat triangles.

fade_color.text: The keywords fade_power, fade_distance and fade_color are specified in the interior statement.

fade_colour.text: The keywords fade_power, fade_distance and fade_color are specified in the interior statement.

fade_distance.text: The keywords fade_power, fade_distance and fade_color are specified in the interior statement.

fade_power.text: In order to get a more realistic effect fade_distance and fade_power keywords followed by float values can be used to model the distance based falloff in light intensity.

falloff.text: The falloff, radius, and tightness keywords control the way that light tapers off at the edges of the cone.

far.text: Written in near { } or far { } they apply to that mouth only and override the portal's.

filter_tags.text: If global_settings appears more than once, the last filter_tags wins.

flatness.text: The four parameters type, flatness, u_steps and v_steps may appear in any order.

focal_point.text: The center of the zone of sharpness is specified by the focal_point vector.

form.text: The form, exterior and interior specify the look of angle used for respectively slow convex (turning side), quick convex (pointy tile) and concave angle (interior angle between many tiles).

frequency.text: The frequency keyword adjusts the number of times that a color map repeats over one cycle of a pattern.

fresnel.text: When used directly in the finish block the fresnel keyword activates Fresnel effects for all of the ambient, diffuse, emission, specular and phong attributes.

function.text: The function statement can be used wherever an image specifier like tga or png may be used.

gather.text: The keyword gather allows you to specify how many photons are gathered at each point during the regular rendering step.

gradient.text: One of the simplest patterns is the gradient pattern.

granite.text: The granite pattern uses a simple 1/f fractal noise function to give a good granite pattern.

gray_threshold.text: The gray_threshold float value grays it down a little, to make your scene more believable.

grey_threshold.text: The gray_threshold float value grays it down a little, to make your scene more believable.

hexagon.text: The hexagon pattern is a block pattern that generates a repeating pattern of hexagons in the x-z-plane.

hf_gray_16.text: A Change as of version 3.7 has deprecated the hf_gray_16 keyword in the global_settings block.

hf_grey_16.text: A Change as of version 3.7 has deprecated the hf_gray_16 keyword in the global_settings block.

hierarchy.text: A blob modifier is any regular object modifier or the hierarchy or sturm keywords.

hollow.text: For example hollow off may be used to force it off.

inside_vector.text: Adding the inside_vector they do have a defined inside.

interior_texture.text: The interior_texture simply allows to specify a separate texture for the interior surface of the object.

interpolate.text: Adding the interpolate keyword can smooth the jagged look of a bitmap.

intervals.text: The classic controls intervals, samples, jitter, aa_level, aa_threshold, confidence, variance and ratio apply to methods 1, 2 and 3, but not to prepared method 4.

inverse.text: When the inverse keyword is used the inside of the shape is flipped to become the outside and vice versa.

ior.text: In earlier versions of POV-Ray, the refraction, ior, and caustics keywords were part of the finish statement but they are now part of the interior statement.

irid.text: This effect is controlled by the irid statement specified inside a finish statement.

irid_wavelength.text: You may adjust the values using the global setting irid_wavelength as follows...

lambda.text: The lambda parameter controls how statistically different the random move of an octave is compared to its previous octave.

linear_spline.text: The default if none is specified is linear_spline.

load_file.text: The keywords save_file and load_file allow you to save and load photon maps.

location.text: Regardless of the projection type all cameras use location, right, up, direction, and other keywords to determine the location and orientation of the camera.

looks_like.text: Using looks_like is as an easy way to override this behavior.

low_error_factor.text: The low_error_factor is a float tuning value which sets the amount that the error bound is dropped during the preliminary image passes.

map_type.text: This option may be changed by adding the map_type keyword followed by an integer number specifying the way to wrap the image around the object.

marble.text: The marble pattern is very similar to the gradient x pattern.

material_map.text: After a material_map statement but still inside the texture statement you may apply any legal texture modifiers.

matrix.text: The matrix keyword can be used to explicitly specify the transformation matrix to be used for objects or textures.

max_gradient.text: When the max_gradient used to find the intersecting point is too high, the render slows down considerably.

max_intersections.text: As of version 3.7 max_intersections has been deprecated, and using it in the global settings blocks now produces a warning at parse time.

max_iteration.text: If none is specified, the default is max_iteration 20.

max_sample.text: This can be sometimes avoided by using the max_sample keyword.

max_trace.text: Consequently, the keyword max_trace followed by an integer value, must be added to the isosurface statement.

max_trace_level.text: If max_trace_level is reached before a non-reflecting surface is found and if ADC has not allowed an early exit from the ray tree the color is returned as black.

maximum_reuse.text: The maximum_reuse parameter works in conjunction with, and is similar to that of minimum_reuse, the only difference being that it is an upper bound rather than a lower one.

media_interaction.text: This behavior can be switched off by using media_interaction off inside the light source statement.

metallic.text: The keyword metallic may be used with phong or specular highlights.

method.text: A method 4 medium in-scatters light with energy-conserving normalisation.

minimum_influence.text: The minimum_influence item gives the least share of the pixel a subsurface hit must carry for method 2 to read its cloud.

minimum_reuse.text: The minimum effective radius ratio is set by minimum_reuse float value.

mix.text: Where media overlap, each medium's mix says how it combines with the media ranked beneath it, and priority raises its rank.

mortar.text: These values may be changed using the optional brick_size and mortar pattern modifiers.

near.text: Written in near { } or far { } they apply to that mouth only and override the portal's.

nearest_count.text: The nearest_count integer value is the minimum number of old radiosity values blended together to create a new interpolated value.

no_image.text: When no_image is used, the object will not be seen by the camera, either directly or through transparent/refractive objects.

no_reflection.text: When no_reflection is used, the object will not show up in reflections.

no_shadow.text: You may specify the no_shadow keyword in an object to make that object cast no shadow.

normal_map.text: The syntax for a normal_map is identical to a pigment_map except you specify a normal in each map entry.

normal_vectors.text: The normal_vectors, uv_vectors, and texture_list sections are optional.

number_of_tiles.text: The number_of_tiles is used to choose the number of basic polygons in the tile while pattern is used to choose amongst the variants.

number_of_waves.text: By default, ten waves are summed but this amount can be globally controlled by changing the number_of_waves setting.

octaves.text: The octaves keyword may be followed by an integer value to control the number of steps of turbulence that are computed.

off.text: By default hollow is off when not specified.

offset.text: The optional offset vector tells how much to translate the pattern each time it repeats.

omega.text: The omega value controls how large each successive octave step is compared to the previous value.

once.text: By adding the once keyword after a file name you can eliminate all other copies of the map except the one at (0,0) to (1,1).

onion.text: The onion is a pattern of concentric spheres like the layers of an onion.

open.text: Adding the optional keyword open after Cap_Radius will remove the end caps and results in a tapered hollow tube like a megaphone or funnel.

orient.text: The orient keyword has been added to area lights in order to better create soft shadows.

parallel.text: The parallel keyword can be used with any type of light source.

pass_through.text: The keyword pass_through causes photons to pass through the object unaffected on their way to a target object.

pattern.text: Of special interest here is the pattern option, that makes it possible to use patterns as functions

pavement.text: The pavement is a pattern which paves the x-z plane with a single polyform tile.

perspective.text: The perspective keyword specifies the default perspective camera which simulates the classic pinhole camera.

phase.text: The phase value causes the map entries to be shifted so that the map starts and ends at a different place.

phong.text: The phong keyword in the finish statement controls the amount of phong highlighting on the object.

phong_size.text: The size of the highlight spot is defined by the phong_size value.

photons.text: With photons it is possible to render true reflective and refractive caustics.

pigment_map.text: You may not use pigment_map or individual pigments with an image_map.

planar.text: The planar pattern creates a horizontal stripe plus or minus one unit above and below the X-Z plane.

point_at.text: The point_at keyword tells the spotlight to point at a particular 3D coordinate.

polarity.text: New in version 3.8 this can be changed via the polarity keyword.

potential.text: New in version 3.8 a potential pattern has been added to define a pattern based on the potential field of a blob or isosurface object.

precision.text: The default if none is specified is precision 20.

premultiplied.text: Additionally the premultiplied parameter may be used to specify the input image alpha handling.

pretrace_end.text: The defaults are 0.08 for pretrace_start and 0.04 for pretrace_end.

pretrace_start.text: To control the radiosity pre-trace gathering step, use the keywords pretrace_start and pretrace_end.

projected_through.text: You can use projected_through with any type of light source.

quadratic_spline.text: The quadratic_spline keyword creates splines that are made of quadratic curves.

quick_color.text: By adding a quick_color to a pigment you tell POV-Ray what solid color to use for quick renders instead of a patterned pigment.

quick_colour.text: By adding a quick_color to a pigment you tell POV-Ray what solid color to use for quick renders instead of a patterned pigment.

quilted.text: The quilted pattern was originally designed only to be used as a normal pattern.

radial.text: The radial pattern is a radial blend that wraps around the +y-axis.

radiosity.text: Radiosity calculations are only made when a radiosity{} block is used inside the global_settings{} block.

radius.text: The falloff, radius, and tightness keywords control the way that light tapers off at the edges of the cone.

ratio.text: The ratio keyword distributes intervals differently between lit and unlit areas.

recursion_limit.text: The recursion_limit is an integer value which determines how many recursion levels are used to calculate the diffuse inter-reflection.

reflection.text: Such mirror-like reflection is controlled by the reflection {...} block in a finish statement.

repeat.text: The repeat warp causes a section of the pattern to be repeated over and over.

right.text: The primary purpose of the up and right vectors is to tell POV-Ray the relative height and width of the view screen.

ripples.text: The ripples pattern was originally designed only to be used as a normal pattern.

rotate.text: You may change the orientation of an object or texture pattern by adding a rotate modifier.

roughness.text: The size of the spot is defined by the value given the roughness keyword.

samples.text: The samples count controls integration noise and shadow quality, not expected brightness.

save_file.text: The keywords save_file and load_file allow you to save and load photon maps.

scale.text: It consists of the keyword scale followed by a vector expression.

scattering.text: The default value if no scattering statement is given is rgb <0,0,0> which means no scattering occurs.

screen.text: Before the screen pattern, a television, a monitor or a picture of another part of the scene took two renders.

shadowless.text: Using the shadowless keyword you can stop a light source from casting shadows.

skein.text: A declared skein can be reused with object { Name } or with skein { Name ...

skein_mesh.text: Each skein_mesh writes one line to the debug stream with its triangles, vertices, open edges, size in bytes, wall and CPU build time, and build threads.

sky.text: You may change the tilt of the camera using the sky vector.

slice.text: A julia fractal object is a 3-D slice of a 4-D object created by generalizing the process used to create the classic Julia sets.

slope.text: The slope pattern uses the normal of a surface to calculate the slope at a given point.

slope_map.text: A slope_map is a normal pattern modifier which gives the user a great deal of control over the exact shape of the bumpy features.

smooth.text: Adding the keyword smooth causes POV-Ray to modify the surface normal vectors of the triangles in such a way that the lighting and shading of the triangles will give a smooth look.

specular.text: The specular keyword in a finish statement produces a highlight which is very similar to phong highlighting but it uses slightly different model.

spherical.text: The spherical pattern creates a one unit radius sphere, with its center at the origin.

spiral1.text: The spiral1 pattern creates a spiral that winds around the z-axis similar to a screw.

spiral2.text: The spiral2 pattern creates a double spiral that winds around the z-axis similar to spiral1 except that it has two overlapping spirals which twist in opposite directions.

split_union.text: With compact objects, without 'empty spaces' split_union off can improve photon gathering.

spotlight.text: However the spotlight keyword can be used to create a cone of light that is bright in the center and falls of to darkness in a soft fringe effect at the edge.

spotted.text: The spotted pattern is identical to the bozo pattern.

sqr.text: The presence of one of the function keywords sqr, cube, etc.

square.text: The square pattern is a block pattern that generates a repeating pattern of squares in the x-z plane.

str.text: Convert float A to a formatted string.

strength.text: The strength parameter of either type of blob component is a float value specifying the field strength at the center of the object.

sturm.text: For example sturm off may be used to force it off.

sys.text: For details about the sys character set option refer to the platform specific documentation.

target.text: First, make your object into a "target." You do this with the target keyword.

texture_list.text: The normal_vectors, uv_vectors, and texture_list sections are optional.

texture_map.text: When used with texture_map or density_map it works the same way.

thickness.text: The thickness keyword represents the film's thickness.

threshold.text: The threshold determines what absolute sampling error (i.e.

tightness.text: The falloff, radius, and tightness keywords control the way that light tapers off at the edges of the cone.

tiles.text: It used the tiles and tile2 keywords to create a checkered pattern of textures.

tiling.text: The tiling pattern creates a series tiles in the x-z plane.

translate.text: It consists of the keyword translate followed by a vector expression.

translucency.text: The translucency color, which can alternatively be a float, determines the strength of the subsurface light transport effect.

transmit.text: You can do this by adding the keyword filter or transmit following the filename.

triangular.text: The triangular pattern is a block pattern that generates a repeating pattern of triangles in the x-z plane.

turbulence.text: Inside the warp statement, the keyword turbulence followed by a float or vector may be used to stir up any pigment, normal or density.

type.text: The keyword type is followed by a float Patch_Type which currently must be either 0 or 1.

u_steps.text: The keywords u_steps and v_steps are each followed by integer values which tell how many rows and columns of triangles are the minimum to use to create the surface, both default to 0.

up.text: In type 3 the up vector determines how many units high the image is.

use_alpha.text: It takes a standard image specification with the option, use_alpha, which works similar to use_color or use_index.

use_color.text: The use_color keyword may be specified to explicitly note that the color methods should be used instead.

use_colour.text: The use_color keyword may be specified to explicitly note that the color methods should be used instead.

use_index.text: If you specify use_index, the bump map uses the color's palette number to compute as the height of the bump at that point.

user_defined.text: Similar to the mesh camera the user_defined camera allows complete control over ray origin and direction, with the advantage of not having to actually load a mesh to function.

utf8.text: The option utf8 is a special Unicode text encoding and it allows you to specify characters of nearly all languages in use today.

uv_vectors.text: With the keyword uv_vectors, the UV coordinates of the corners can be controlled for bicubic patches and standard triangle mesh.

v_steps.text: The keywords u_steps and v_steps are each followed by integer values which tell how many rows and columns of triangles are the minimum to use to create the surface, both default to 0.

variance.text: The variance value specifies an acceptable tolerance on the variance of the samples taken so far.

vstr.text: Convert vector A to a formatted string.

warp.text: The warp statement is a pattern modifier that is similar to turbulence.

water_level.text: The optional water_level parameter may be added after the file name.

waves.text: The waves pattern was originally designed only to be used as a normal pattern.

wood.text: The wood pattern consists of concentric cylinders centered on the z-axis.

wrinkles.text: The wrinkles pattern was originally designed only to be used as a normal pattern.

x.text: The built-in vector identifiers x, y, and z provide much greater readability for your scene files when used in vector expressions.

y.text: The built-in vector identifiers x, y, and z provide much greater readability for your scene files when used in vector expressions.

z.text: The default three parameters are x, y and z.

acos.code: asinh | cos | acos | cosh | acosh | tan | atan |tanh |

acosh.code: asinh | cos | acos | cosh | acosh | tan | atan |tanh |

asin.code: sqr | cube | exp | reciprocal | sin | asin | sinh |

atan.code: asinh( FLOAT ) | atan( FLOAT) | atanh( FLOAT) |

auto.code: let Bend = refraction { function { -0.01*(x+detail) } function { 0.005 } detail auto };

back.code: front [on | off] | back [on | off] | no_lights [on | off] | pigment { PIGMENT_BODY } |

brilliance.code: emission COLOR | brilliance Amount | phong [albedo] Amount | phong_size Amount |

checker.code: pigment { checker color rgb <0.8, 0.8, 0.8> color rgb <0.25, 0.3, 0.4> }

colour.code: method INT | colour COLOR | pigment { PIGMENT } |

cos.code: for (I = 1 to 100000) { S = S + sin(I) * cos(I / 3); }

cosh.code: cosh( FLOAT ) | degrees( FLOAT ) | exp( FLOAT ) |

debug.code: fn G() { debug("pov4 debug statement\n"); warning("pov4 warning statement"); return 1; }

difference.code: difference { box { <-1, -1, -1>, <1, 0.5, 1> } Tree(0.8) translate <0, 0, 3> pigment { rgb Clamp(1.5) } }

error.code: if (max_extent(Scaled).x != 2) { error("bare comparison in a block item differs"); }

error_bound.code: subsurface { method 2 spacing FLOAT error_bound FLOAT memory FLOAT }

exr.code: exr | gif | hdr | jpeg | pgm | png | pot | ppm | sys | tga | tiff

face_indices.code: face_indices { N, ...[for (I = 0 to N - 1) { <I, mod(I + 1, N), N> }] }

front.code: front [on | off] | back [on | off] | no_lights [on | off] | pigment { PIGMENT_BODY } |

global.code: fn Bump() { global Counter = Counter + 1; return Counter; }

hdr.code: exr | gif | hdr | jpeg | pgm | png | pot | ppm | sys | tga | tiff

height_field.code: height_field { function 200,200 { pattern { bozo } } translate -0.5 scale 10 pigment {rgb 1} }

iff.code: exr | gif | hdr | iff | jpeg | pgm | png | ppm | sys | tga | tiff

inherit.code: sphere { 0, 0.5 pigment { color rgb <0.3, 1, 0.2> } tags { ...Extra, inherit } }

ior_mix.code: sphere { 0, 0.5 pigment { rgbf 1 } interior { ior atmosphere ior_mix replace } }

keys.code: for (K in keys(Words)) { if (K != "plain") { sphere { <0, 0, 2>, strlen(K) * 0.2 } } }

lemon.code: lemon { <0,-20,0>, 0, <0,20,0>, 0, 30 texture { pigment { color srgb <1,0,0> }} translate x*-12 sturm }

light_group.code: light_group { LIGHT_GROUP LIGHT | LIGHT_GROUP OBJECT | LIGHT_GROUP [LIGHT_GROUP MODIFIER] }

memory.code: subsurface { method 2 spacing FLOAT error_bound FLOAT memory FLOAT }

minimum_influence.code: finish { subsurface { translucency COLOR minimum_influence FLOAT } }

no_lights.code: portal { sphere { <-1.5, 1.1, 0>, 0.75 } to { translate 3 * x } no_lights }

none.code: sphere { x * 1.5, 0.5 pigment { color rgb <0.2, 0.3, 1> } tags { none } }

number_of_sides.code: number_of_sides SIDES_VALUE | number_of_tiles TILES_VALUE | pattern PATTERN_VALUE |

number_of_tiles.code: number_of_sides SIDES_VALUE | number_of_tiles TILES_VALUE | pattern PATTERN_VALUE |

object.code: object { Ball translate x * 2.5 scale Scale(1.5) }

orthographic.code: camera { orthographic location <0, 0, -6> look_at 0 right x*4 up y*3 }
